dimensions.name: Requirements clarification
dimensions.description: Clarifies suggestion behavior, ranking inputs, freshness, locales, and privacy constraints.

levels.1: Restates the prompt without separating retrieval, ranking, or freshness.
levels.2: Lists basic prefix suggestions but omits ranking signals, locales, or privacy.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states assumptions about personalization and freshness.
levels.4: Also prioritizes features, defines acceptable staleness, and connects privacy or abuse concerns to concrete product constraints.

dimensions.name: Back-of-envelope estimation
dimensions.description: Derives QPS, peak load, index size, and update volume from the stated traffic.

levels.1: Repeats the numbers without deriving any capacity requirement.
levels.2: Computes average QPS but ignores peak traffic, index memory, or update rates.
levels.3: Estimates average and peak QPS, top-K index size, and the rate of index updates.
levels.4: Also estimates cache hit share, hot-prefix concentration, rebuild duration, and the headroom needed for live events.

dimensions.name: API and data model
dimensions.description: Defines the suggestion contract and a prefix index or equivalent retrieval structure.

levels.1: No clear API or index structure.
levels.2: Shows a prefix endpoint but omits ranking fields, locale, or top-K storage.
levels.3: Defines request/response shapes and a trie or index that stores ranked candidates per prefix.
levels.4: Also covers caching headers, versioning, overlay data, blocklists, and how display text differs from normalized query text.

dimensions.name: High-level architecture
dimensions.description: Separates ingestion, aggregation, index building, serving, and caching.

levels.1: A single box with no update pipeline.
levels.2: Names services but does not explain how observations become suggestions.
levels.3: Shows ingestion, aggregation, index build/publish, serving, and caching with clear responsibilities.
levels.4: Also explains immutable index versions, warm-up, rollback, and how trending or personalization layers attach to the base index.

dimensions.name: Deep dives
dimensions.description: Explains ranking, index refresh, and hot-prefix serving in implementable detail.

levels.1: No deep dive beyond the API.
levels.2: Covers ranking or refresh but leaves hot-prefix behavior and failure handling vague.
levels.3: Covers ranking signals, index rebuild and publish, and hot-prefix caching or replication.
levels.4: Also explains score decay, abuse resistance, versioned rollout, and the exact behavior when a shard or index is unavailable.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares freshness, latency, cost, cacheability, and privacy choices.

levels.2: Names one trade-off without linking it to the design.
levels.3: Compares meaningful options such as precomputed top-K vs query-time ranking, or batch vs streaming updates.
levels.4: Also explains when the chosen option would be wrong and how the team would detect and revisit it.

dimensions.name: Communication and failure handling
dimensions.description: Presents a clear design with monitoring, privacy, and degraded modes.

levels.2: Understandable but omits several failure modes or privacy safeguards.
levels.3: Explains the flow clearly and covers stale indexes, shard loss, hot prefixes, and monitoring.
levels.4: Also covers fallback suggestions, abuse controls, privacy-preserving telemetry, and a concise summary of the key decisions.
